paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God is with His people in the middle of the shaking, not just after it's over. The singers call Him "an ever-present help in times of trouble" (Psalm 46:1). Mountains toppling, seas roaring, nations raging, and the song still says "we will not fear" (Psalm 46:2). I'm a stamper who got shoved in a junk drawer, and I can tell you this: that kind of calm doesn't come from the weather. It comes from WHO is standing next to you.

Notice what the song leans on, and it's the same line twice: "The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress" (Psalm 46:7, 11). The singers don't say the trouble is small, and they don't pretend nothing is shaking. They say God is within the city of God, so "she will not be moved" (Psalm 46:5). Their steadiness is not in how strong they feel. It's in who is with them.

Then God Himself speaks: "Be still and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted over the earth" (Psalm 46:10). Being still here is not about being calm on your own. It's about knowing who is God, and He is over every storm, and every nation, and every loud thing that's got you rattled. So when your week starts shaking, baker, don't hunt for something to hold onto. Be still, and remember who's holding YOU.
